{{Trail|Alchemy}} [[Category:Skyrim-Magic]] [[Category:Skyrim-Magic-Effects]]
The following tables provide lists of all the [[Skyrim:Alchemy|alchemical]] effects and the [[Skyrim:Ingredients|ingredients]] with that effect. Details on the various effects can be found on the [[Skyrim:Magical Effects|Magical Effects]] page.  Green effects are positive effects and are used to create drinkable '''potions'''.  Red effects are negative effects used to create '''poisons''' that can be applied to weapons.  Ingredients listed in '''bold''' have that effect as their first, meaning that eating a sample of that ingredient will provide a small version of that effect.

== Potion Strengths ==
The last three columns of the following table provide the magnitude, duration, and cost (gold) of a ''standard'' potion if crafted at 100 Alchemy skill, without any perks.  These are ''not'' the maximum strengths of a potion: they can be increased if alchemy perks are unlocked and also by [[Skyrim:Fortify Alchemy|fortifying alchemy]] skill.  With 100% Fortify Alchemy (the maximum possible without custom enchantments) and all Alchemy perks, most potions and poisons will be five times stronger (6.25 times stronger for restoration potions).  Even larger enhancements are possible with custom enchantments.

Values in italics (for example, the duration of many potions) are values that are not visible in-game, and in most cases do not have an effect on gameplay.  However, those values are still relevant in determining the cost of the potion.

=== Non-Standard Ingredients ===
Several effects (most notably Damage Health) have ingredients that produce non-standard potion strengths.  Those ingredients are noted in the following table by including symbols summarizing how those ingredients alter the potion.  For example:
* [[Skyrim:River Betty|River Betty]] ({{Effect Mult|mag|2.5}}): Damage Health potions that include River Betty will have a magnitude 2.5 times greater than a standard Damage Health potion (e.g., 30 magnitude at alchemy 100).  The gold cost of the potion is also affected, but the factor is not shown on this page (see [[Skyrim:Damage Health|Damage Health]] for details).
* [[Skyrim:Nirnroot|Nirnroot]] ({{Effect Mult|val|12.6}}): Damage Health potions that include Nirnroot will have a gold cost 12.6 times larger than a standard potion, even though the magnitude of the potion is the same.  (The internal value for the duration of the potion has been changed, but that duration has no effect on gameplay other than through the gold cost of the potion).

When using non-standard ingredients, the effect properties are determined '''only by the highest priority ingredient''' for that effect, where the ingredient priority is believed to be the Cost for the effect, as listed for each item in the Creation Kit.  The ingredients in the following table are all listed in decreasing priority, so the top-most ingredient is always the one that determines the properties.  If River Betty and Nirnroot are combined, the potion will have the exact same properties as a potion made using River Betty and Deathbell or River Betty and Falmer Ear.  This also means that ingredients with weaker effect strengths, such as [[Skyrim:Ectoplasm|Ectoplasm]] and Nightshade for Fortify Destruction, are only relevant if combined with another weak ingredient.  Ectoplasm combined with any Fortify Destruction ingredient other than Nightshade yields a standard-strength Fortify Destruction potion.

=== Damage Health Gold cost Bug ===

There's a bug that affects gold calculation for most ingredients with [[Skyrim:Damage Health|Damage Health]]. Instead of calculating gold cost based on a 0-second duration (which is treated as 10 seconds), many Damage Health ingredients use a 1-second duration. The ingredients [[Skyrim:River Betty|River Betty]], [[Skyrim:Nirnroot|Nirnroot]], and [[Skyrim:Emperor Parasol Moss|Emperor Parasol Moss]]{{DB}} are exceptions to this rule.

=== Strength Equations ===
{|class="wikitable collapsible collapsed"
!Helper functions used in effect strength calculations:
|-
| style="padding:0" |
{{Pre|style=margin:0|<nowiki>function AlchemistPerk() {
    if (Player.HasPerk "000c07cd") return 100 // Alchemist perk rank 5
    else if (Player.HasPerk "000c07cc") return 80 // Alchemist perk rank 4
    else if (Player.HasPerk "000c07cb") return 60 // Alchemist perk rank 3
    else if (Player.HasPerk "000c07ca") return 40 // Alchemist perk rank 2
    else if (Player.HasPerk "000be127") return 20 // Alchemist perk rank 1
    else return 0
}
 
function PhysicianPerk(</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/MGEF|MGEF]]<nowiki> mgef) {
    restoreHealth = "00042503" // Restore Health (MagicAlchRestoreHealth)
    restoreMagicka = "00042508" // Restore Magicka (MagicAlchRestoreMagicka)
    restoreStamina = "00042503" // Restore Stamina (MagicAlchRestoreStamina)
    physicianPerk = Player.HasPerk "00058215" // Physician perk
    KYWD kwda[] = mgef.</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/KYWD#Including Keywords|KWDA]]<nowiki> // effect keywords
    if (physicianPerk and kwda.ContainsAny(restoreHealth, restoreMagicka, restoreStamina)) return 25
    else return 0
}
 
function BenefactorPerk(</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/MGEF|MGEF]]<nowiki> mgef) {
    beneficial = "000F8A4E" // Beneficial Effect (MagicAlchBeneficial)
    benefactorPerk = Player.HasPerk "00058216" // Benefactor perk
    isPotion = not EPAlchemyGetMakingPoison
    KYWD kwda[] = mgef.</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/KYWD#Including Keywords|KWDA]]<nowiki> // effect keywords
    if (benefactorPerk and isPotion and kwda.Contains(beneficial)) return 25
    else return 0
}
 
function PoisonerPerk(</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/MGEF|MGEF]]<nowiki> mgef) {
    harmful = "00042509" // Harmful Effect (MagicAlchHarmful)
    poisonerPerk = Player.HasPerk "00058217" // Poisoner perk
    isPoison = EPAlchemyGetMakingPoison
    KYWD kwda[] = mgef.</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/KYWD#Including Keywords|KWDA]]<nowiki> // effect keywords
    if (poisonerPerk and isPoison and kwda.Contains(harmful)) return 25
    else return 0
}

function PowerFactor(</nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/MGEF|MGEF]]<nowiki> mgef) {
    ingredientMult = GetGameSetting fAlchemyIngredientInitMult // 4.0
    skillFactor = GetGameSetting fAlchemySkillFactor // 1.5
    alchemySkill = Player.GetBaseActorValue Alchemy
    fortifyAlchemy = Player.GetActorValue AlchemyMod// the sum of all active </nowiki>[[Skyrim:Fortify Alchemy|Fortify Alchemy]]<nowiki> effects
    alchemistPerk = AlchemistPerk()
    physicianPerk = PhysicianPerk(mgef)
    benefactorPerk = BenefactorPerk(mgef)
    poisonerPerk = PoisonerPerk(mgef)
    return ingredientMult * (1 + (skillFactor - 1) * alchemySkill / 100) *
            (1 + fortifyAlchemy / 100) * (1 + alchemistPerk / 100) *
            (1 + physicianPerk / 100) * (1 + benefactorPerk / 100 + poisonerPerk / 100)
    // alternative result, wrong:
    //     ingredientMult * skillFactor ^ (alchemySkill / 100) *
    //      (1 + fortifyAlchemy / 100) * (1 + alchemistPerk / 100) *
    //      (1 + physicianPerk / 100) * (1 + benefactorPerk / 100 + poisonerPerk / 100)
}</nowiki>}}
|}

{|class="wikitable collapsible collapsed"
!The magnitude, duration, and gold value of a potion effect are calculated from:
|-
| style="padding:0" |
{{Pre|style=margin:0|[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/MGEF|MGEF]]<nowiki> effect = </nowiki>[[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/INGR|ingredient]]<nowiki>.Effect.EFID
powerFactor = PowerFactor(effect)

magnitude = ingredient.Effect.EFIT.Magnitude
if (effect.DATA.Flags.NoMagnitude) magnitude = 0
magnitudeFactor = 1
if (effect.DATA.Flags.PowerAffectsMagnitude) magnitudeFactor = powerFactor
magnitude = round(magnitude * magnitudeFactor)

duration = ingredient.Effect.EFIT.Duration
if (effect.DATA.Flags.NoDuration or duration < 0) duration = 0
durationFactor = 1
if (effect.DATA.Flags.PowerAffectsDuration) durationFactor = powerFactor
duration = round(duration * durationFactor)

magnitudeFactor = 1
if (magnitude > 0 ) magnitudeFactor = magnitude
durationFactor = 1
if (duration > 0 ) durationFactor = duration / 10
value = floor(effect.DATA.BaseCost * (magnitudeFactor * durationFactor) ^ 1.1)
</nowiki>}}
|}

{|class="wikitable collapsible collapsed"
!The magnitude of a potion is calculated from:
|-
| style="padding:0" |
{{Pre|style=margin:0|<nowiki>Magnitude =  round(Base_Mag *
             4 *                          (Game setting fAlchemyIngredientInitMult)
            (1+(Alchemy_Skill/200)) *   (1.5 is the game setting fAlchemySkillFactor; this is technically 1+(fAlchemySkillFactor-1)*(Alchemy_Skill/100))
            (1 + Fortify_Alchemy/100) *
            (1 + Alchemist_Perk/100)  *
            (1 + Physician_Perk/100)  *
            (1 + Benefactor_Perk/100  + Poisoner_Perk/100) *
            (1 + Seeker of Shadows/100))</nowiki>}}
|}

For potions where the duration varies instead of magnitude, the same equation is applied to the duration, using <code>Base_Dur</code> instead of <code>Base_Mag</code>. Currently duration only varies for Invisibility, Paralysis, Slow, and Waterbreathing; for all other effects: <code>Duration = Base_Dur</code>. The values used in these equations are:
* <code>Base_Mag</code> and <code>Base_Dur</code> are the strengths for the single strongest ingredient being used in the potion.  In the game data, these base values are listed in the ingredient's [[Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/INGR|EFIT]] field.  The standard base values used for each effect are listed on each effect page, as well as details about the base values for any non-standard ingredients.
* <code>Alchemy_Skill</code> is your character's alchemy skill (15-100)
* <code>Fortify_Alchemy</code> is the sum of all active [[Skyrim:Fortify Alchemy|Fortify Alchemy]] enchantments
* <code>Alchemist_Perk</code> is the enhancement from the [[Skyrim:Alchemist|Alchemist]] perk (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, or 100)
* <code>Physician_Perk</code> is the enhancement from the [[Skyrim:Physician|Physician]] perk (0 or 25).  This value is only set to 25 if your character has unlocked the perk ''and'' it is being applied to a [[Skyrim:Restore Health|Restore Health]], [[Skyrim:Restore Magicka|Restore Magicka]], or [[Skyrim:Restore Stamina|Restore Stamina]] effect
* <code>Benefactor_Perk</code> is the enhancement from the [[Skyrim:Benefactor|Benefactor]] perk (0 or 25).  This value is only set to 25 if your character has unlocked the perk ''and'' it is being applied to a beneficial effect in a potion.
* <code>Poisoner_Perk</code> is the enhancement from the [[Skyrim:Poisoner|Poisoner]] perk (0 or 25).  This value is only set to 25 if your character has unlocked the perk ''and'' it is being applied to a negative effect in a poison.
**(Only one of <code>Benefactor_Perk</code> or <code>Poisoner_Perk</code> is ever non-zero).
* <code>Seeker of Shadows</code> is the enhancement from the [[Skyrim:Powers#Abilities|Seeker of Shadows]] ability (0 or 10) from [[Skyrim:Dragonborn|Dragonborn]] that adds +10% to potion magnitude.

The gold cost of a potion is calculated from:
  Gold_cost = floor( Base_Cost * max(Magnitude^1.1,1) * ((Duration/10)^1.1 if Duration else 1) )
If the magnitude or duration is zero, the corresponding term disappears from the equation, i.e.:
  Gold_cost (When Magnitude = 0) = floor( Base_Cost * max((Duration/10)^1.1,1) )
  Gold_cost (When Duration = 0)  = floor( Base_Cost * (Magnitude^1.1) )
  Gold_cost (When Duration = 0 and Magnitude = 0, which is never true in vanilla)  = floor( Base_Cost )
If the magnitude or duration is not displayed in game, that does '''not''' necessarily mean that the value is zero.  The game still has an internal value for each parameter (based on the ingredient's <code>Base_Mag</code> and <code>Base_Dur</code>) which is used in this calculation.  A clear-cut example of these hidden values at work is the Cure Disease potion, which has a higher monetary value when brewed to a higher "magnitude", despite having both a fixed effect and a fixed duration in practice.  These internal values are listed in the following table.

=== Multiple-Effect Potions ===
If a potion has multiple effects, the magnitude, duration, and gold cost of each effect is separately determined according to the [[#Strength Equation|above equations]].  The total gold cost of the potion is the sum of the costs of the individual effects.

The effect with the largest individual gold cost is the effect that controls the overall properties of the mixture.  That effect is used for naming, and it determines whether the result is considered to be a potion or a poison.  The determination of the strongest effect is actually done before the perks are factored into the gold cost (i.e., having the Benefactor and/or Poisoner perk does not alter whether a mixture is a poison or a potion).

Additional adjustments that are made include:
* The [[Skyrim:Benefactor|Benefactor]] perk only applies to effects in potions — beneficial side-effects of a poison are not enhanced.
* The [[Skyrim:Poisoner|Poisoner]] perk only applies to effects in poisons — negative side-effects of a potion are not enhanced.
* If the [[Skyrim:Purity_(perk)|Purity]] perk has been unlocked, the properties of all negative effects in a potion will be set to zero (and positive effects in a poison will be set to zero).  This means that the gold cost of the potion will be reduced.

==Effect List==
Any potion effect will be affected by Alchemy level, perks, enchantments, etc, and this effect will either go to its magnitude ''or'' its duration (never both, and never neither). The other attribute is fixed, and is always the same regardless of outside factors such as level, perks, or enchantments. The variable attribute is noted in below by having a green background. The majority of effects have a fixed duration and a variable magnitude.

Note that Cure Disease and Cure Poison have variable magnitudes which have no impact when drank (these always cure all diseases and remove all poisons, respectively), but ''does'' impact the gold value of the potion.  Note also that Damage Magicka and the three Ravage effects have non-zero durations which likewise have no impact when applied to the target - the first is instantaneous and the latter three are permanent until cured - but ''do'' impact the gold value of the potion.
